source.title: Beyond Interpretability: When, Why, and How Sparse Autoencoders Enable Label-Free Visual Steering
source.authors: Gerasimos Chatzoudis; Zhuo-Wei Li; Gemma E. Moran; Hao Wang; Dimitris N. Metaxas

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some equations and table layouts are flattened, but the feature-activation results used here are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Extends SAE feature analysis to CLIP visual encoders and reports evidence about what sparse features recover; it does not test the LLM-specific part of V4.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses superposition in related work but does not test toy-model superposition, capacity accounts of polysemanticity, SAE feature completeness or stability, or feature dimensionality. Main steering-accuracy and FVU results concern downstream steering and reconstruction reliability, not those claims. Appendix A's CUB feature-activation results are included for V4.
record.test_reason: The paper uses top-k SAEs on CLIP vision encoders as a tool for a label-free steering method (VS2). Its results are steering accuracy, FVU-gated reliability and ablations of its own method. The only feature-level evidence (Appendix A, Table 5) covers two hand-picked SAE features shown as illustrations. There is no baseline, no population-level rate and no LLM, so it does not test V4, which concerns LLMs, or any other version. Superposition appears only in related work.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SAE latents give a practical, label-free intervention space for steering CLIP (VS2). They frame steering as centroid-deviation with an FVU reliability gate, and identify a reconstruction-vs-task saliency gap. They explicitly do not claim human interpretability of SAE features and cite feature absorption.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains top-k SAEs on CLIP visual activations and applies SAE-based steering and feature analysis; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports steering sensitivity to hyperparameters, layers, SAE capacity, and dataset, but these are not tests of the listed superposition versions.

fits_no_version.finding: In CLIP ViT SAEs on CUB-200, two selected features align with a gull-like grouping (feature 511, near 0% on unrelated classes) and a cross-class throat/eye attribute (feature 3067).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs on vision-encoder activations yield some interpretable concept-aligned features (vision analogue of V4).

fits_no_version.finding: Steering vectors from SAEs of different width and sparsity have cosine similarity ranging from about 0.14 to 0.96 (Table 16), while downstream accuracy varies by less than 1 point (Table 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-derived directions depend on dictionary size and sparsity (related to V5 stability, but measured on steering vectors, not features).

record.problems: Feature evidence is limited to two selected CUB-200 SAE features and top-activating-image analyses; it does not establish feature completeness or stability, and the paper does not evaluate LLMs. No uncertainty estimates are reported for these feature-frequency results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional Appendix A feature-frequency entries were left out. Steering accuracy, FVU, and steering-vector cosine results were excluded because they do not measure the listed superposition versions.

untested.parts: No toy models; no sparsity-dependent transition or geometry analysis.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions for important features.
No analysis of the origins of polysemantic neurons.
No LLMs are studied. No measurement of features spread across neurons. SAE recovery in a vision encoder is shown only for two hand-picked features.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are not evaluated. Feature absorption is mentioned only via a citation.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T3/V4 'supports' label is dropped. The system is a CLIP vision encoder, not an LLM. The Table 5 entries are hand-picked illustrative features with no baseline or population rate.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions; overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure, and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
The paper analyzes CLIP visual encoders, not LLMs; it does not measure feature spreading across neurons. Its evidence is limited to selected SAE features in CUB-200.
Completeness, stability, and canonical status of SAE features are not evaluated.
The paper does not determine whether superposed features are one-dimensional or multidimensional.

reader_labels.condition: Selected SAE features in CUB-200 visual representations
reader_labels.reason: The reported class frequencies show feature 511 concentrated on gull-like classes and feature 3067 activating across multiple classes; this supports recovery of coherent visual concepts by an SAE in this setting (rows r1–r20).
